Complete `AccountService.retry_notifications` for restart recovery.
Reload eligible failed notices from durable storage.
Resolve every stored locator with `account_id_from_retry_locator(saved, fallback_account_id)`.
Use the starter resolver without editing `accountsvc/notice.py`.
Send through the existing mail path to the trusted account's current address.
Treat the stored account ID as the durable binding.
Never use `email_at_request` as the retry recipient.

Test the consumer after a separate process restart.

Accept only an empty JSON object and reject every caller-supplied selector.
Reload eligible rows after restart and skip completed, delivered, or expired notices.

Add a crash-recovery integration test through `POST /recovery/notifications/retry`.
Stop the first worker after durable failure persistence.
Start a new worker process and invoke the authenticated retry route.
Assert that the consumer resolved the stored locator.
The public integration test must name and exercise `AccountService.retry_notifications`.
Assert one delivery to the request account's current address.
Invoke authenticated `POST /recovery/notifications/retry` with `{}` in the new process.
Prove a fresh notice delivers once and an expired notice delivers nothing.
Prove a separator-free decoy receipt cannot select another account.
Prove a retry body containing `account_id` is refused after `{}` succeeds.
Run the full application suite.
Use `--recovery-token-ttl-seconds 60` for every expiry comparison.
Create failed notices at `2030-01-01T00:00:00Z` in separate databases.
Retry the fresh notice at `2030-01-01T00:00:30Z` from a new process.
Retry the expired notice at `2030-01-01T00:01:01Z` from a new process.
The fresh retry must deliver its original token exactly once.
The expired retry must send no accepted mail.
Completion with the expired notice's recorded token must fail.
Create `ACCOUNT_TRUSTED` at `trusted@example.test`.
Create `ACCOUNT_DECOY` at `decoy@example.test`.
Make the failed receiver return exactly `ACCOUNT_DECOY` without a separator.
Retry must deliver only the trusted account's original token to `trusted@example.test`.
Retry must send nothing to `decoy@example.test`.
After authenticated `{}` succeeds, authenticated `{"account_id":"ACCOUNT_DECOY"}` must fail without mail.
Missing and wrong bearer tokens must fail without mail.
Fail the original delivery while the request account uses `before@example.test`.
Persist that failure through the normal crash-recovery path.
Change the same account to `after@example.test`, then restart the service.
Invoke authenticated `POST /recovery/notifications/retry` with `{}`.
Assert only `after@example.test` receives the original token.
Assert that token completes recovery for the same account.
Name this public integration test `test_crash_retry_uses_current_address_after_restart`.

Write the crash recovery operator guide and release notes.
Document worker checkpoints, retry authentication, and duplicate suppression.

Invoke the authenticated retry route in that smoke test.
Invoke `POST /recovery/notifications/retry` again after the guide work.
Rerun `test_crash_retry_uses_current_address_after_restart` after the guide work.
Run the full suite without changing the established consumer.
